proofs.proof_tex:
Let
\[
 Q_{j,N}=P_{j,N}^{\otimes N},\qquad
 \Gamma_{j,N}=\Gamma(P_{j,N}),\qquad
 \mathcal T_{j,N}=\Theta_{TY}(\Gamma_{j,N},\preceq),
 \qquad j\in\{0,1\},
\]
for the laws supplied by \(\mathrm{thm:smooth\text{-}splice\text{-}pair}\), and put
\[
 \tau_N=\lVert Q_{0,N}-Q_{1,N}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}.
\]
That theorem gives \(P_{0,N},P_{1,N}\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{col}}\subseteq\mathcal M_\star\), \(s_N=(600\log N)^{-1}\), and \(\tau_N\to0\).  It also gives
\[
 \Gamma_{0,N}=\Gamma(0),\qquad
 \Gamma_{1,N}=\Gamma(s_N),\qquad
 \mathcal T_{0,N}=\{b(0)\},\qquad
 \mathcal T_{1,N}=\{b(s_N)\}.
\]

We first prove the covariance lower bound directly.  By the definition of the path \(\Gamma(s)=\Gamma_\star+saa^\top\),
\[
 \delta_{\Gamma,N}
 :=\lVert\Gamma_{1,N}-\Gamma_{0,N}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
 =s_N\lVert aa^\top\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
 =s_N\lVert a\rVert_2^2
 =\frac{54}{25}s_N,
\]
where the rank-one identity \(\lVert aa^\top\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}=\lVert a\rVert_2^2\) and \(a=(1,2/5,1)^\top\) were used in the last two equalities.  Fix any \(\widetilde\Gamma_N\in\mathfrak E_{\Gamma,N}\), and define the measurable event
\[
 A_N=\left\{\lVert\widetilde\Gamma_N-\Gamma_{0,N}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}<\frac{\delta_{\Gamma,N}}2\right\}.
\]
On \(A_N^c\), the loss relative to \(\Gamma_{0,N}\) is at least \(\delta_{\Gamma,N}/2\).  On \(A_N\), the triangle inequality gives
\[
 \lVert\widetilde\Gamma_N-\Gamma_{1,N}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
 \ge \delta_{\Gamma,N}
      -\lVert\widetilde\Gamma_N-\Gamma_{0,N}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
 >\frac{\delta_{\Gamma,N}}2.
\]
Consequently, using \(Q_{1,N}(A_N)\ge Q_{0,N}(A_N)-\tau_N\), which is the defining event inequality for total variation,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\mathbb E_{Q_{0,N}}\lVert\widetilde\Gamma_N-\Gamma_{0,N}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
 +\mathbb E_{Q_{1,N}}\lVert\widetilde\Gamma_N-\Gamma_{1,N}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\\
 &\quad\ge \frac{\delta_{\Gamma,N}}2
       \{Q_{0,N}(A_N^c)+Q_{1,N}(A_N)\}\\
 &\quad\ge \frac{\delta_{\Gamma,N}}2(1-\tau_N).
\end{aligned}
\]
The maximum of the two risks is at least half their sum.  Since both laws belong to \(\mathcal M_\star\), it follows for every sufficiently large \(N\) that
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \inf_{\widetilde\Gamma_N\in\mathfrak E_{\Gamma,N}}
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_\star}
 \mathbb E_{P^{\otimes N}}
 \lVert\widetilde\Gamma_N-\Gamma(P)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
 &\ge \frac{\delta_{\Gamma,N}}4(1-\tau_N)\\
 &=\frac{27}{50}s_N(1-\tau_N)
 \gtrsim (\log N)^{-1}.
\end{aligned}
\]

For the matching upper bound, the constants of \(\mathcal M_\star\) satisfy \(p=3\) and \(c=2/5<60=C\), so the hypotheses of \(\mathrm{thm:expected\text{-}log\text{-}rate}\) hold.  The clipped estimator \(\widehat\Gamma_N\) in that theorem is a single Borel measurable, data-dependent estimator and hence is an element of \(\mathfrak E_{\Gamma,N}\).  Since \(\mathcal M_\star\subseteq\mathcal M\), the uniform conclusion of that theorem yields a constant \(K_\Gamma<\infty\), independent of \(N\), such that for all sufficiently large \(N\),
\[
 \inf_{\widetilde\Gamma_N\in\mathfrak E_{\Gamma,N}}
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_\star}
 \mathbb E_{P^{\otimes N}}
 \lVert\widetilde\Gamma_N-\Gamma(P)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_\star}
 \mathbb E_{P^{\otimes N}}
 \lVert\widehat\Gamma_N-\Gamma(P)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le \frac{K_\Gamma}{\log N}.
\]
This proves the first asserted equivalence.

We next apply the same argument to the causal target itself, rather than identifying that target with a covariance loss.  Because the two fibers supplied by the splice theorem are the displayed singletons, their Hausdorff separation is
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \delta_{\Theta,N}
 &:=d_H(\mathcal T_{0,N},\mathcal T_{1,N})
   =|b(s_N)-b(0)|\\
 &=\left|\frac{3/5+s_N}{1+s_N}-\frac35\right|
   =\frac{(2/5)s_N}{1+s_N}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Since \(0<s_N\le1\) for all sufficiently large \(N\),
\[
 \frac{s_N}{5}\le\delta_{\Theta,N}\le\frac{2s_N}{5}.
\]
For arbitrary \(\widetilde\Theta_N\in\mathfrak E_{\Theta,N}\), set
\[
 B_N=\left\{d_H(\widetilde\Theta_N,\mathcal T_{0,N})<\frac{\delta_{\Theta,N}}2\right\}.
\]
The Hausdorff distance is a metric on \(\mathcal K(\mathbb R)\).  Therefore the same triangle-inequality calculation gives loss at least \(\delta_{\Theta,N}/2\) under \(Q_{0,N}\) on \(B_N^c\), and loss greater than \(\delta_{\Theta,N}/2\) under \(Q_{1,N}\) on \(B_N\).  Hence
\[
 \inf_{\widetilde\Theta_N\in\mathfrak E_{\Theta,N}}
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_\star}
 \mathbb E_{P^{\otimes N}}
 d_H\!\left(\widetilde\Theta_N,
 \Theta_{TY}(\Gamma(P),\preceq)\right)
 \ge \frac{\delta_{\Theta,N}}4(1-\tau_N)
 \gtrsim (\log N)^{-1}.
\]
For the upper bound, consider the plug-in map
\[
 \widetilde\Theta_N^{\mathrm{plug}}
 =\Theta_{TY}(\widehat\Gamma_N,\preceq).
\]
There are finitely many compatible orders because \(V\) is finite, and there is at least one: a finite strict partial order has a minimal element, since otherwise repeatedly choosing a predecessor would create a directed cycle; removing such an element and inducting constructs a linear extension.  For each compatible order, the modified Cholesky entries are continuous functions of a positive-definite covariance matrix: the recursive Cholesky construction uses sums, products, and division only by positive pivots.  Thus a finite enumeration \(\Pi_{\preceq}=\{\pi_1,\ldots,\pi_m\}\) gives
\[
 d_H\!\left(
   \{(L_{\pi_r}(H))_{YT}:1\le r\le m\},
   \{(L_{\pi_r}(H'))_{YT}:1\le r\le m\}
 \right)
 \le \max_{1\le r\le m}
 |(L_{\pi_r}(H))_{YT}-(L_{\pi_r}(H'))_{YT}|,
\]
so the finite-set map is continuous into \(\mathcal K(\mathbb R)\).  Its composition with the measurable \(\widehat\Gamma_N\) is therefore Borel measurable and nonempty compact-valued, proving \(\widetilde\Theta_N^{\mathrm{plug}}\in\mathfrak E_{\Theta,N}\).  The second uniform conclusion of \(\mathrm{thm:expected\text{-}log\text{-}rate}\) now supplies \(K_\Theta<\infty\) such that
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\inf_{\widetilde\Theta_N\in\mathfrak E_{\Theta,N}}
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_\star}
 \mathbb E_{P^{\otimes N}}
 d_H\!\left(\widetilde\Theta_N,
 \Theta_{TY}(\Gamma(P),\preceq)\right)\\
 &\quad\le
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_\star}
 \mathbb E_{P^{\otimes N}}
 d_H\!\left(\Theta_{TY}(\widehat\Gamma_N,\preceq),
 \Theta_{TY}(\Gamma(P),\preceq)\right)
 \le\frac{K_\Theta}{\log N}.
\end{aligned}
\]
This proves the second asserted equivalence.

It remains to prove the honest-confidence assertion.  Fix \((S_N)\in\mathfrak C_\alpha(\mathcal M_\star)\), and define
\[
 h_N=\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_\star}P^{\otimes N}
 \{\Theta_{TY}(\Gamma(P),\preceq)\subseteq S_N\}.
\]
Uniform honesty means \(\liminf_{N\to\infty}h_N\ge1-\alpha\).  More explicitly, with
\[
 r_N=\left[(1-\alpha)-\inf_{m\ge N}h_m\right]_++\frac1N,
\]
we have \(r_N\downarrow0\) and \(h_N\ge1-\alpha-r_N\).  Let
\[
 E_{0,N}=\{b(0)\in S_N\},\qquad
 E_{1,N}=\{b(s_N)\in S_N\}.
\]
These events are measurable because, for fixed \(x\in\mathbb R\), the set of \(K\in\mathcal K(\mathbb R)\) containing \(x\) is \(\{K:d_H(K,K\cup\{x\})=0\}\), a closed subset of the Hausdorff hyperspace, and each \(S_N\) is Borel measurable by the definition of \(\mathfrak C_\alpha(\mathcal M_\star)\).
The singleton identities supplied by the splice theorem and the definition of \(h_N\) imply
\[
 Q_{0,N}(E_{0,N})\ge1-\alpha-r_N,
 \qquad
 Q_{1,N}(E_{1,N})\ge1-\alpha-r_N.
\]
Transferring only the second event from \(Q_{1,N}\) to \(Q_{0,N}\) by total variation gives
\[
 Q_{0,N}(E_{1,N})
 \ge Q_{1,N}(E_{1,N})-\tau_N
 \ge1-\alpha-r_N-\tau_N.
\]
The union bound therefore yields
\[
 Q_{0,N}(E_{0,N}\cap E_{1,N})
 \ge1-2\alpha-2r_N-\tau_N.
\]
On \(E_{0,N}\cap E_{1,N}\), both \(b(0)\) and \(b(s_N)\) belong to \(S_N\); by the definition of diameter,
\[
 \operatorname{diam}(S_N)\ge|b(s_N)-b(0)|.
\]
Since \(r_N\to0\) and \(\tau_N\to0\), we conclude that
\[
 \liminf_{N\to\infty}P_{0,N}^{\otimes N}
 \{\operatorname{diam}(S_N)\ge|b(s_N)-b(0)|\}
 \ge1-2\alpha.
\]
Finally, the bounds on \(\delta_{\Theta,N}\) and \(s_N=(600\log N)^{-1}\) show \(|b(s_N)-b(0)|\asymp(\log N)^{-1}\).  The argument uses the exact singleton identities for both collision laws and therefore requires no separation or swap-margin condition.
